title: The Cosmic Distance Scale Calibration (H0 Anchors)
bottleneck: The entire local H0 measurement rests on a handful of geometric anchors (NGC 4258 maser, LMC eclipsing binaries, Gaia parallaxes), each with its own systematics. Disagreements between Cepheid, TRGB, and surface-brightness-fluctuation routes at the few-percent level suggest unrecognized errors somewhere in the ladder's foundations. Gaia parallaxes are revolutionizing the calibration, but bright-star systematics and zero-point offsets remain under investigation.
why_it_blocks: The Hubble tension cannot be adjudicated until the ladder's anchors are beyond reproach. Every rung's systematics propagate directly into H0, so anchor disagreements of even 1% matter enormously.
current_state: Gaia DR4 parallaxes and JWST anchor re-observations are tightening calibrations, but inter-method offsets persist. A fully independent distance ladder based on gravitational waves would bypass these anchors, though it needs many more events.
